Relevant Jest output (npm test -- --verbose): - Suite: "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" — all tests passed - Suite: "Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" — all tests passed - Suite: "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" — all tests passed
Example tests (from tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts): - Valid cases: - "[REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid story file reference" — `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` - "[REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension" — `// @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md` - "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix" — `// @story ./docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - Invalid cases: - Missing file: expects `messageId: "fileMissing"` with path `docs/stories/missing-file.story.md` - Wrong extension: expects `messageId: "invalidExtension"` - Path traversal: expects `messageId: "invalidPath"` for `../outside.story.md` - Absolute path: expects `messageId: "invalidPath"` for `/etc/passwd.story.md` - Configurable paths: - Honors custom storyDirectories: validates bare filename using `storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"]` - allowAbsolutePaths true/false behavior for absolute .story.md inside project - requireStoryExtension=false allows `.md` story files when they exist in configured storyDirectories - Project boundary: - Rejects absolute paths resolving outside project root, even when allowAbsolutePaths and storyDirectories are set - Ensures misconfigured storyDirectories outside project produce `invalidPath` diagnostics - Error handling: - storyExists returns false and does not throw when fs.existsSync/statSync throw EACCES/EIO - Rule reports `fileAccessError` with error details when fs errors occur
Core rule behavior (src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts): - Parses comments, finds lines starting with '@story', extracts the path, and validates via processStoryPath(). - Uses performSecurityValidations() to check absolute paths and traversal and report `invalidPath` when disallowed. - Enforces .story.md extension when requireStoryExtension is true, reporting `invalidExtension` otherwise. - Uses normalizeStoryPath() (with cwd and storyDirectories) to build candidate paths and get existence; handles project boundaries via handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(). - Reports `fileMissing` for non-existent files and `fileAccessError` for fs-error statuses, including the offending path and underlying error message.
Utility behavior (src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts): - buildStoryCandidates(): resolves './' or '../' paths directly against cwd; for bare names, tries cwd and then cwd + each storyDirectories entry. - checkSingleCandidate(): wraps fs.existsSync/statSync in try/catch, categorizing results as 'exists', 'missing', or 'fs-error'; caches results in fileExistStatusCache. - getStoryExistence(): aggregates across candidates, preferring 'exists' > 'fs-error' > 'missing', never throwing. - storyExists(): returns boolean based on getStoryExistence(). - normalizeStoryPath(): returns candidates, a boolean exists, and the full existence result. - enforceProjectBoundary(): ensures candidate paths are under the normalized cwd.
Helpers (src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts): - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(): determines whether any candidate is inside or outside project. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(): uses enforceProjectBoundary and candidates/existenceResult to decide when to report `invalidPath` for out-of-project references. - performSecurityValidations(): rejects disallowed absolute paths and traversal that escape cwd, calling reportInvalidPath and halting processing when unsafe.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements in docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md are implemented and covered by passing tests.
Mapping to acceptance criteria: - Core Functionality: The valid-story-reference ESLint rule validates that @story paths reference existing .story.md files using normalizeStoryPath() and getStoryExistence(), reporting fileMissing for missing files. Tests explicitly cover both valid existing references and missing targets. - Quality Standards: The rule is a well-structured RuleModule with meta, messages, and JSON schema. All filesystem interactions are centralized in storyReferenceUtils, wrapped in try/catch and never throwing, matching ESLint best practices for safety. - Integration with 005.0: This rule assumes syntactically valid annotations and only parses '@story ' lines from comments. It operates on top of annotation format validation rather than redoing it, consistent with the dependency on 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - User Experience: Error messages fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, and fileAccessError clearly indicate which path is problematic and in the case of filesystem errors include the underlying error text, giving actionable feedback. - Error Handling: storyReferenceUtils handles EACCES/EIO and other fs errors by returning status 'fs-error' and never throwing; the rule converts these into fileAccessError diagnostics. Tests simulate these errors and assert that no exceptions are thrown and that correct diagnostics are produced. - Documentation: The story file itself documents path resolution rules, examples, and configuration; the implementation is richly annotated with @story/@req JSDoc comments linking code back to this story, effectively embedding the specification.
Mapping to specific requirements: - REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE: Implemented via buildStoryCandidates(), checkSingleCandidate(), getStoryExistence(), normalizeStoryPath(), and reportExistenceStatus()/reportExistenceProblems(); verified by tests for valid references and the 'missing file' case expecting fileMissing. - REQ-ERROR-HANDLING: Implemented by wrapping fs calls in checkSingleCandidate(), surfacing fs-error status and detailed error data, and by reporting fileAccessError in the rule. Dedicated tests cover permission and I/O error scenarios and confirm the rule does not crash. - REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION: handleComment() and validateStoryPath() parse comment text, identify '@story' lines, and extract the path token; all RuleTester scenarios rely on this to trigger the rule. - REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION: Cwd-aware resolution using context.cwd or process.cwd, plus buildStoryCandidates() logic and configurable storyDirectories, is tested via ./ paths, bare names, and storyDirectories-based resolution. - REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION: performSecurityValidations() and enforceProjectBoundary()/handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() prevent disallowed absolute paths and traversal outside the project, with tests proving invalidPath is reported for those scenarios. - REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION: fileExistStatusCache and short-circuiting in checkSingleCandidate()/getStoryExistence() provide caching to avoid repeated disk I/O during a lint run. - REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY: enforceProjectBoundary() plus handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() ensure that only paths within the normalized project root are considered valid; tests cover absolute external paths and misconfigured storyDirectories. - REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS: Rule options (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension) are defined in the JSON schema, read in create(), and exercised in multiple tests to verify directory-based resolution, optional absolute paths inside the project, and relaxed extension rules.
Given the implemented rule, utilities, configuration options, extensive targeted tests, and passing Jest run, the story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully satisfied.
